newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Wienerberger in 3 bln ATS real estate deal.
newsitem.headline: Wienerberger in 3 bln ATS real estate deal.

text.p: Austrian brick maker Wienerberger said on Thursday it had sold a key Vienna office and retail complex to Immofinanz for more than three billion schillings, realising a net gain of 500 million schillings.

The group also said it had acquired a 150 million schilling stake in Immofinanz, one of Austria's leading real estate units managed by unlisted Constantia Privatbank, describing the purchase as a "long-term investment".
In a statement released ahead of a news briefing, the group said the sale was part of its strategy to concentrate on its core businesses of bricks and pipes.
Wienerberger is considered to be the world's biggest brick maker.

"(The sale) will enable Wienerberger to focus on industrial expansion in the core business -- building materials," it said. "Property which is not required for operations is developed and sold after potential increases in value have been realised."
Wienerberger said the deal would contribute substantially to earnings growth in the current year.
"Combined with the 25 percent increase in profits for 1997, the profit and capital structure of the Wienerberger group will improve decisively this year," it said.
Immofinanz would register an increase in rental income of about 300 million schillings this year, it added.

Business Park Vienna, the Austrian capital's largest office and business centre, has some 86,500 square metres of usable space and includes a hotel, shops and service facilities. Wienerberger said the complex was fully rented.
Wienerberger said Immofinanz had acquired the complex "because rental prices for office space in Vienna are expected to increase over the mid-term."
Wienerberger is majority controlled by Austria's Creditanstalt and Belgium's Koramic.
Koramic said it would book a net current gain of 350 million Belgian francs on the sale by its Austrian partner.
Wienerberger shares, part of the key ATX stock index, were suspended from trading on the Vienna stock exchange until 0900 GMT. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 274
